```text
# PR #3356: Patch: drop the square shadow behind the card face's cost gem

Closes #3329

The card face's cost gem no longer draws a square shadow behind its hexagon. I checked this only through CSS text tests, not in a browser, and the before/after screenshots the issue asks for are not attached.

## What changed

- **`apps/web/src/cards/cards.css`**: `.cf .cost-gem` now declares `box-shadow: none;` beside its other resets (`border`, `border-radius`, `background`). `board.css` is untouched, so board tiles keep their round gem and its shadow. The hexagon's own `::before` `drop-shadow` is also untouched.
- **`apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts`** (new), three tests. It reads the stylesheets as text, as `borders.test.ts` does.
  1. `cards.css` has exactly one `.cf .cost-gem` rule, and its `box-shadow` is `none`.
  2. No rule ending in `.cost-gem` (`::before` excluded) in the face's stylesheets declares a `box-shadow` other than `none`. It also asserts at least 8 such rules were found, so it can't pass by matching nothing.
  3. `.cf .cost-gem::before` keeps its `clip-path: polygon(…)` and its `filter: drop-shadow(…)`.

No ruling is involved, so there is no `spec/` note and no R-number. The change is presentation only.

## How I tested it

- **Before the fix:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts` gave 1 failed and 2 passed. The failing one was test 1 (`expected null to be 'none'`), so it does pin the reset.
- **After the fix:** the new file plus `borders.test.ts`, `CardFace.test.tsx`, `cosmetics.test.tsx`, `glitch.test.tsx`, `foil.test.ts` and `typography.test.ts` gave 7 files, 181 tests, all passed.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` exited 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts` exited 0, with no `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore`.
- **Full web run:** `pnpm exec vitest run --project web` gave 468 files passed and 8523 tests passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.
  - I excluded `src/audio/**`, `src/fx/**` and `src/cards/art/convention.test.ts`, as the harness's web check does.
  - I did not look into the skipped test.
- `git status` shows only `cards.css` and `costGem.test.ts`.

## Red or not run

Nothing was red. I did not run these:
- The Rust checks (`cargo fmt`, clippy, cargo tests, `catalog`, `patches` and `spec check`), because no Rust or spec file changed.
- The e2e specs.
- The plain `pnpm --dir apps/web test` script. I ran vitest directly, and built the WebAssembly module first with `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`. `apps/web/src/wasm/pkg` is git-ignored.
- The five required CI checks, which only run on the pull request.

## For a person

- **Screenshots:** the acceptance asks for before/after screenshots of a spell face and a minion face in the inspect view, attached to the PR. I have no GitHub access and did not boot the client. Please attach them, either with the issue's own Chromium check or from `/dev/hotseat` with a card inspected.

## Decisions the issue left open

- I chose a unit test over a Cypress component spec, because the harness runs it and I could run it here. The alternative, asserting `getComputedStyle(.cf .cost-gem).boxShadow` in a browser, needs a browser run I did not have.
- The plan said to check that nothing else in `cards/` relies on the shadow. I did that through test 2, which sweeps the face's stylesheets, including `cosmetics.css`, `glitch.css` and `stamps.css`. In `cards/`, only `cards.css` (seven rules) and `glitch.css` (one rule, `text-shadow` only) have a rule ending in `.cost-gem`, and none sets `box-shadow`. Test 2 does not cover `board.css`.
- I made no departure from the plan.

## Worth a second look

- Test 2's floor of 8 rules is deliberately low. A later change that legitimately removes a gem rule should lower it in the same PR.
- The CSS parser in the test is a flat `{…}` regex. It also matches rules inside `@media` and `@container` blocks, as `CardFace.test.tsx` and `TermTip.test.tsx` already rely on.
```

**Issue #3329 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3329: Patch: drop the square shadow behind the card face's cost gem
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

## What players see

On a card face (hand preview, inspect view, almanac), there's a faint square box behind the hexagonal mana crystal in the top-left corner. It shows up most clearly where it overlaps the frame and the art window. It was reported on Call to Chaos (Training-Grounds Edition), but it shows on every face.

## Cause

There are two rules for `.cost-gem`:

- `apps/web/src/game/board.css:1233` is the older round gem for board tiles. It sets `border`, `border-radius: var(--radius-round)`, `background` and **`box-shadow: var(--shadow-2)`** (`0 4px 12px` black at 50%).
- `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css:324` (`.cf .cost-gem`) restyles the gem as a hexagon for `CardFace.tsx` and `MinionFace.tsx`. It resets `border: 0`, `border-radius: 0` and `background: none`, but it never resets `box-shadow`.

So the face gem keeps board.css's shadow, now drawn around a square box (radius 0) instead of a circle. The hexagon itself is the clipped `::before` (`cards.css:349`), which already has its own `filter: drop-shadow(...)` that follows the hex outline. The square shadow behind it is the extra box.

I checked this with a standalone page that loads the app's real stylesheets in Chromium:
- `getComputedStyle(.cf .cost-gem).boxShadow` is `rgba(0,0,0,0.5) 0px 4px 12px 0px` and `border-radius` is `0px`.
- Setting `box-shadow: none` on the gem makes the square disappear, and the hexagon's own drop shadow stays.

## Fix

- Add `box-shadow: none;` to `.cf .cost-gem` in `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css` with the other resets (border, border-radius, background). Leave board.css's `.cost-gem` alone, since board tiles still use it.
- Check that nothing else in `cards/` (`cosmetics.css`, `glitch.css`, `stamps.css`, the full-art and minion-layout rules) relies on that shadow being there.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A web unit test, or a component/pixel spec under `e2e/` if that fits better, that pins `.cf .cost-gem` to no box shadow. It can be as simple as asserting `box-shadow: none` sits in the `.cf .cost-gem` rule, so the reset can't be dropped again.
- [ ] Screenshot of a spell face and a minion face in the inspect view, before and after, attached to the PR. The square is gone and the hexagon still has its own drop shadow.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test` and the five required checks are green.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42311617385)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

The card face's cost gem (hand preview, inspect view, almanac) stops drawing a square shadow behind its hexagon. `.cf .cost-gem` in `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css` gets `box-shadow: none;` beside its other resets. A web unit test pins that reset so it can't be dropped again. The hexagon's own `::before` drop shadow stays, and `board.css`'s round `.cost-gem` for board tiles stays untouched. The issue's before/after screenshots are covered under **Open questions**.

I checked the stylesheets under `apps/web/src/cards/` with a read-only script. Only `cards.css` (seven rules) and `glitch.css` (one rule, `text-shadow` only) have a selector ending in `.cost-gem`. None sets `box-shadow`, so nothing in `cards/` relies on the shadow. That covers `cosmetics.css`, `stamps.css` and the full-art and minion-layout rules.

## Files to touch

| File | Status | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css` | change | In the `.cf .cost-gem` rule (line 324), add `box-shadow: none;` after `background: none;`. |
| `apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts` | new | A vitest file that reads the sheets as text and pins the reset (3 tests, below). |

Do not touch:
- `apps/web/src/game/board.css`: board tiles still use its `.cost-gem` shadow.
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`.
- Any crate, `spec/`, or `crates/cards/patches/`.
- `apps/web/src/wire/`.

No spec section or ruling governs this. It is presentation only, so there is no ruling note, no `proven_in` entry and no R-number in the test. `CLAUDE.md` rules 3, 4 and 9 are not touched, because no number is added and no pure crate changes. The new test is named after the issue, like `typography.test.ts`'s `#2123` tests.

## Steps

1. **Write the test first**, in the new file `apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts`. Use this content:

```ts
// #3329: the face's cost gem is a hexagon (cards.css's `.cf .cost-gem`), so it draws no box shadow of
// its own. board.css's round `.cost-gem` has one (`--shadow-2`); on the face's square, radius-0 box it
// showed as a faint square behind the crystal. The hexagon's `::before` keeps its `drop-shadow`, which
// follows the outline. Vitest stubs CSS imports and jsdom paints nothing, so this reads the sheets as
// text (borders.test.ts does the same). Presentation only: no ruling, so no R number.

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { readSheet } from "../test/setup.ts";

/** Every sheet of the face and its marks that could style the gem. */
const FACE_SHEETS = [
  "cards.css",
  "cosmetics.css",
  "glitch.css",
  "stamps.css",
  "cardstate.css",
  "marks.css",
  "keywords.css",
  "dormant.css",
  "tallies.css",
  "setmark.css",
  "inspect/inspect.css",
] as const;

/** A sheet's rules (at any depth) as selector and body, comments stripped so a comment naming a property proves nothing. */
function rules(file: string): { selector: string; body: string }[] {
  const css = readSheet(`src/cards/${file}`).replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "");
  return [...css.matchAll(/([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}/g)].map((match) => ({ selector: (match[1] ?? "").trim(), body: match[2] ?? "" }));
}

/** The value of `property` in a rule's body, or null when it declares none. */
function declared(body: string, property: string): string | null {
  const match = new RegExp(`(?:^|[;\\s])${property}\\s*:\\s*([^;]+)`).exec(body);
  return match === null ? null : (match[1] ?? "").trim();
}

describe("#3329 the face's cost gem shadow", () => {
  it("#3329 .cf .cost-gem resets box-shadow, so board.css's round gem shadow is not drawn round its square box", () => {
    const gem = rules("cards.css").filter((rule) => rule.selector === ".cf .cost-gem");
    expect(gem, "the face's one gem rule").toHaveLength(1);
    expect(declared(gem[0]?.body ?? "", "box-shadow")).toBe("none");
  });

  it("#3329 no rule of the face's sheets puts a box shadow back on the gem's box", () => {
    let seen = 0;
    for (const file of FACE_SHEETS) {
      for (const rule of rules(file)) {
        for (const part of rule.selector.split(",")) {
          // The gem's own box: `.cost-gem`, with attribute selectors at most (not its `::before`).
          if (!/\.cost-gem(\[[^\]]*\])*$/.test(part.trim())) continue;
          seen += 1;
          const shadow = declared(rule.body, "box-shadow");
          expect(shadow === null || shadow === "none", `${file}: ${part.trim()} sets box-shadow: ${shadow ?? ""}`).toBe(true);
        }
      }
    }
    expect(seen, "the sweep found the gem's rules").toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(8);
  });

  it("#3329 the hexagon keeps its own drop shadow, which follows its outline", () => {
    const hex = rules("cards.css").filter((rule) => rule.selector === ".cf .cost-gem::before");
    expect(hex, "the hexagon's one rule").toHaveLength(1);
    expect(declared(hex[0]?.body ?? "", "clip-path")).toContain("polygon(");
    expect(declared(hex[0]?.body ?? "", "filter")).toContain("drop-shadow(");
  });
});
```

   `readSheet` is the helper in `apps/web/src/test/setup.ts` that `keywordVisuals.test.tsx` imports. It takes a path from `apps/web`, hence the `src/cards/` prefix. The `rules` and `declared` helpers are copied in miniature from `apps/web/src/cards/borders.test.ts`. The repo duplicates them per test file, so do not extract a shared module.

2. **Run the new test before the fix** with the command under **Tests**. The first test must fail, because `declared(...)` returns `null` rather than `"none"`. The other two must pass. If the first does not fail, the test is not pinning the reset: fix the test, not the CSS.

3. **Apply the fix** in `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css`, in the `.cf .cost-gem` rule. The rule currently reads `border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: none; color: #fff;`. Insert one declaration between the `background` and `color` lines:

```css
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: none;
  box-shadow: none;
  color: #fff;
```

   Do not edit the comment above the rule, `::before`, or any other rule. Do not touch `board.css`.

4. **Re-run the new test**, then the neighbouring card CSS tests listed under **Tests**. All must pass.

5. **Run the checks under Done when.**

## Tests

New file `apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts`, three tests:
- `#3329 .cf .cost-gem resets box-shadow, so board.css's round gem shadow is not drawn round its square box`: cards.css has exactly one rule whose selector is `.cf .cost-gem`, and its `box-shadow` is `none`. This is the test that fails without the fix.
- `#3329 no rule of the face's sheets puts a box shadow back on the gem's box`: across the `FACE_SHEETS` stylesheets, no rule ending in `.cost-gem` (attribute selectors allowed, `::before` excluded) declares a `box-shadow` other than `none`. It also asserts the sweep matched at least 8 rules, so it can't pass by matching nothing. I counted 8 today: seven in `cards.css` and one in `glitch.css`.
- `#3329 the hexagon keeps its own drop shadow, which follows its outline`: the `.cf .cost-gem::before` rule keeps its `clip-path: polygon(…)` and a `filter` containing `drop-shadow(`.

Commands (the first run builds the WebAssembly module via `pretest`, which takes minutes):

```
pnpm --dir apps/web test src/cards/costGem.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web test src/cards/borders.test.ts src/cards/CardFace.test.tsx src/cards/cosmetics.test.tsx src/cards/glitch.test.tsx src/cards/foil.test.ts src/typography.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm --dir apps/web test
```

The second command covers every existing test that reads `cards.css` as text. The `cosmetics.test.tsx` ones check `.cf .cost-gem`'s `z-index`, and `typography.test.ts` lists its `font-variant-numeric`. Neither should be affected.

## Done when

- [ ] `.cf .cost-gem` in `apps/web/src/cards/cards.css` declares `box-shadow: none;` with the other resets. `board.css` is unchanged.
- [ ] `apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts` exists. Its first test failed before the CSS change (step 2) and all three pass after.
- [ ] The neighbouring card CSS tests listed above pass.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm --dir apps/web test` are green.
- [ ] `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/cards/costGem.test.ts` is clean, with no `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore`.
- [ ] `git status` shows only the two files above.
- [ ] The harness's own checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests (with `apps/web/src/wire` unchanged) and the web tests. No Rust or spec file is touched, so those should be unaffected.
- [ ] The final report names any check that was red or not run.

## Risks

- **Other shadow users:** `.cf .cost-gem` styles the gem in `CardFace.tsx` and `MinionFace.tsx`, so the reset also reaches board minions, which is intended. `.zone .card-unit .cost-gem` is `display: none` and `.board … > .card .cost-gem` is `visibility: hidden`. Both are old `.card` or `.card-unit` markup, not `.cf`, so neither is affected.
- **Specificity:** `box-shadow: none` on `.cf .cost-gem` (two classes) beats board.css's `.cost-gem` (one class) regardless of sheet order. No later face rule sets it again, as the second test enforces.
- **Test fragility:** the parser is a flat `{…}` regex (it matches rules inside `@media`/`@container` blocks, as `CardFace.test.tsx` and `TermTip.test.tsx` already do). The `seen >= 8` floor is deliberately low. If a later PR legitimately removes a gem rule, lower it with the change.
- **Not a rules change:** no determinism, replay, hidden-information or wire concern. `crates/` and `apps/web/src/wire/` are not involved.

## Open questions

- **Screenshots.** The acceptance asks for before/after screenshots of a spell face and a minion face in the inspect view, attached to the PR. The night bot has no GitHub access and cannot attach images, so a person has to attach them: the issue's own Chromium check, or `/dev/hotseat` with a card inspected. The builder should say in its report that the screenshots are not attached, and need not boot the client for them (the `ui-walkthrough` skill says that costs minutes, and the unit test already pins the CSS).
- **E2E spec.** The issue allows a unit test or a component spec. I chose the unit test because it runs in the harness's checks and the builder can verify it. A Cypress assertion on `getComputedStyle(.cf .cost-gem).boxShadow` would need a browser run the builder may not have.
- **Difficulty.** The rule gives `difficulty:medium`: one CSS declaration and one test file, no engine, AI, cross-crate or migration work.
````
